caveats: The source inoculum is 1e6 CFU/mL, not the historical 1e8 denominator. Neither inoculum nor net CFU loss estimates cumulative drug-induced killing.
A 2,4,6 h sampling mean is not a 4 h point. No ISP:beta-lactam ratio is formed from these unmatched summaries.
3.5-7 is a conditional latent-yield range, not a measured interval or CI. Whole-blood TNF, plasma endotoxin and culture free LPS are different estimands.
The filamentation release coefficient is an assumption; zero and doubled values are included in joint_robustness.json.

Carbapenems filament at sub-MIC concentrations and release heavily there (Tsuji 2003: 0.1x vs 10x MIC raises free LPS 88-fold for doripenem and 48-fold for meropenem), so assigning the kill-independent term to PBP-3 agents alone is a structural assumption, not an observation. scripts/ds_filament_structure.py quantifies what relaxing it would cost.
analysis1_yield_table.interpretation: Matched culture observations support an agent-specific release difference among bactericidal drugs. They do not identify commensurable fg/CFU yields. Keep source observations, latent model coefficients and cross-agent transfer assumptions separate.
analysis1_yield_table.mechanism: The mechanism is PBP-3-SPECIFIC CELL-WALL DAMAGE, not filamentation as such. Trautmann 1998 settles this: ciprofloxacin induces filaments, with killing curves nearly identical to the beta-lactams, yet releases as little free LPS as the carbapenems -- so morphology does not predict release. Meropenem points the same way: it binds PBP-3 as well as PBP-2 and still releases little, so it is the DOMINANT PBP-3 specificity of the cephalosporins that matters. Filamentation is a marker of the relevant lesion, not its cause.
analysis1_yield_table.net_change_matched_note: Ceftazidime against a carbapenem at EQUAL NET bacterial change, the only source reporting viable counts with the LPS endpoint. Equal net change is NOT equal cumulative drug-induced killing, and in the 0.1x MIC pair both arms GREW, so that pair is matched on growth. These bracket the assumed 3.5-7 range but are three pairs from one experiment at one timepoint with no replicate dispersion; the range is NOT refitted to them.
analysis1_yield_table.coefficient_status: All fg/CFU entries are nominal scale conventions, not measurements

analysis2_dual_pathway.observation_to_explain: Jackson & Kropp 1992: sub-MIC ceftazidime released LPS in amounts MATCHING those at 1, 2 and 50x MIC, without significant lysis.
analysis2_dual_pathway.conclusion: NECESSITY IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and an earlier version of this entry claimed it was. On the attributable-exposure endpoint the lysis-only structure already reproduces the stated observation: its 0.5x/50x ratio is 0.963, i.e. matching, while the dual structure overshoots at 6.78. What the comparison shows is that the two structures are DISTINGUISHABLE below the MIC -- 7.0-fold in absolute attributable exposure at 0.5x -- so the term is identifiable in principle by an experiment measuring release and viable counts together below the MIC. Deciding between them requires joint fitting at the source's own sampling times under an observation model, which has not been done.
analysis2_dual_pathway.superseded_conclusion: Retained so the error is traceable: 'A lysis-only model cannot reproduce that observation: with Y_filament = 0 the predicted sub-MIC release collapses ... the kill-independent pathway is therefore REQUIRED.' The collapse is relative to the dual model's own sub-MIC value, not to the supra-MIC values the observation compares against.
analysis2_dual_pathway.counter_evidence: Prins 1995 (E. coli, whole blood) found 0.5x MIC comparable to untreated with little agent separation, which the dual-pathway model does NOT reproduce. The two held-out sources conflict; Y_filament is plausibly organism-dependent and bounded above by Prins. Unresolved -- see PHASE3_VALIDATION.md section 6.

analysis3_matched_exposure.claim: At matched %fT>MIC the two agents achieve nearly equal bacterial killing (see kill_difference_log10 per row; matching exposure does not guarantee equal killing when profile shapes differ), and the PBP-3 agent imposes the higher danger-signal cost. The ratio is reported as a range over the assumed 3.5-7x yield range.

fT_pct.description: percent fT>MIC (the efficacy standard for beta-lactams)

cost_offset_at_matched_index.note: cost ratio ceftazidime/meropenem at matched %fT>MIC, by log-interpolating each agent's cost against the index over the range the two libraries share. One yield configuration, so this is narrower than analysis 3's span, which also propagates the assumed yield range.

mass_balance_identity.statement: k_ds * AUC_D = a * [Y_lysis * int(kill*B_rep dt) + Y_filament * int(phi*B_rep dt)] - [D(T) - D(0)], with D the attributable danger signal and a the common focus/translocation conversion factor
mass_balance_identity.consequence: The proposed yield-weighted killed-biomass index is the leading term of the right-hand side, so its near-perfect rank correlation with AUC_DS is an algebraic consequence of the compartment's mass balance, NOT independent evidence of predictive performance. Its practical value is that it needs only a standard PK/PD simulation and a yield table.

analysis4_cost_index.interpretation: Across agents, the established efficacy indices rank inflammatory cost poorly or perversely, because they are agent-blind: two regimens with the same %fT>MIC differ several-fold in cost (see analysis3 for the range) depending only on which agent delivers that exposure. Weighting cumulative killed biomass by the agent's yield recovers the ranking using only a standard PK/PD simulation plus a yield table, which is the practical proposal.

coverage.note: Arms are skipped where the dose solving the exposure target falls outside the 10-16000 mg search bracket, so the map is not fully populated and the summaries below are over the arms that exist, not over the full grid.

analysis5_divergence_map.pooling_caveat: The pooled failing/controlled medians mix both agents and so carry the yield difference as well as the exposure effect. The per-agent figures in 'by_agent' are the ones to report.
analysis5_divergence_map.interpretation: NO divergent step was found anywhere on the AVAILABLE arms of this map: raising exposure never raised inflammatory cost in any evaluated step. Two regimes explain it. ABOVE stasis, cost is nearly FLAT in exposure, because rapid control leaves little kill-regrowth turnover: almost all of the cumulative killing is of the burden already present, so how fast it is killed barely matters. This is a REGIME-SPECIFIC explanation, not a general bound -- cumulative killed biomass is NOT bounded by the starting burden in a growing population; see analysis3.killed_over_initial_burden, which exceeds 1. BELOW stasis, therapy fails, the burden grows, and sustained kill-regrowth turnover makes cost rise by orders of magnitude. The practical reading is that no within-agent trade-off appeared in the scenarios evaluated: under-dosing is bad for both objectives at once.
analysis5_divergence_map.hypothesis_amendment: This FALSIFIES the clause in DESIGN.md section 1 that 'the regimen that maximizes bacterial killing is not necessarily the one that minimizes host inflammatory injury' -- for regimens of a single agent above stasis, maximizing killing also minimizes inflammatory cost. The divergence the study is about lives BETWEEN agents at matched exposure, not between regimens of one agent. The hypothesis survives in its agent-comparison form and must be restated in that form.
analysis5_divergence_map.caveat: The reported endpoint is attributable AUC_DS, which is an upstream LINEAR compartment and so has no mathematical saturation ceiling; the receptor-occupancy ceiling noted in PHASE2_BUILD.md bounds the (unreported) cytokine layer only. The empirical limits of the danger-signal layer at failing-therapy burdens are separate and remain unvalidated, so the MAGNITUDE of the failing-therapy cost should be read as indicative and its DIRECTION as the result.

analysis6_predictions.prediction: At matched %fT>MIC against the same organism, ceftazidime and meropenem achieve indistinguishable bacterial killing but ceftazidime produces strictly greater danger-signal exposure and cytokine induction.
analysis6_predictions.quantitative: predicted cost ratio 4-9x (interval reflects the revised 3.5-7x yield range; see PHASE5B_AGENT_EFFECT.md)
analysis6_predictions.test: An in-vitro PK-simulation run of two matched-%fT>MIC regimens with serial free-LPS and whole-blood cytokine induction. This is a single experiment and it is the decisive one.
analysis6_predictions.falsified_if: cytokine induction is equal, or ordered the other way, at matched exposure and matched kill.

analysis6_predictions.prediction: %fT>MIC does not rank regimens by inflammatory cost across agents, whereas cumulative killed biomass weighted by agent yield does.
analysis6_predictions.quantitative: Spearman rho vs modelled cost: %fT>MIC -0.38, best candidate 'yield_weighted_kill' +1.00
analysis6_predictions.test: Rank a regimen library by each index and compare against measured cytokine induction.
analysis6_predictions.falsified_if: %fT>MIC ranks measured inflammatory cost as well as the yield-weighted index.

analysis6_predictions.prediction: The kill-independent (filamentation) pathway is activated by UNDER-EXPOSURE, not by reduced susceptibility as such. Reduced susceptibility matters only because, at a fixed dose, it causes under-exposure.
analysis6_predictions.quantitative: the filamentation share of release is a function of %fT>MIC alone: 0.39 at a 20% fT>MIC target and <=0.01 at 80%, and it is IDENTICAL at MIC x1 and MIC x64 when the dose is raised to hold %fT>MIC fixed
analysis6_predictions.test: Measure free LPS and cytokine induction for ceftazidime against isolates of graded MIC, once at a fixed dose and once at doses adjusted to hold %fT>MIC constant. The prediction is that the MIC effect disappears in the second arm.
analysis6_predictions.falsified_if: release per unit kill depends on the isolate's MIC even at matched %fT>MIC.
analysis6_predictions.note: This supersedes the Phase 1 statement, which was made at FIXED DOSE and so confounded susceptibility with exposure. The underlying numbers are unchanged; the attribution is corrected.

analysis6_predictions.prediction: Y_filament is organism-dependent: substantial in P. aeruginosa, small in E. coli.
analysis6_predictions.quantitative: the two held-out sources differ on this; the model reproduces Jackson & Kropp and contradicts Prins
analysis6_predictions.test: Repeat one sub-MIC release protocol on both organisms in one laboratory with one assay.
analysis6_predictions.falsified_if: both organisms behave the same, in which case one of the two published results is an assay artefact.

analysis6_predictions.prediction: No survival difference is predicted. The model predicts inflammatory exposure, and Simpson 2000 observed a significant endotoxin difference with identical mortality.
analysis6_predictions.quantitative: n/a -- this is a statement of scope
analysis6_predictions.falsified_if: n/a; recorded so the model is not over-read.

stasis_thresholds.note: A competent host needs less drug to hold the organism static, so the immunocompetent thresholds are the lower pair. Craig reports 30-40% fT>MIC for cephalosporins in neutropenic animals; the comparable figures here are the immune-free ones.
